title: Human-Centered AI and Healthy Longevity at CDHI
summary: A June keynote explored how intelligent systems can remain meaningful and usable in older adults' everyday lives.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: Chorong Park reflected on a June keynote with the Centre for Digital Health Interventions in an August 19, 2026, post. CDHI's event announcement identifies the keynote date as June 1, distinguishing the research visit from the later reflection.

Her presentation connected ELARA's work on human-centered AI, socially assistive robots, voice interaction, and technology for aging. The central question was how intelligent, adaptive systems can also be trustworthy, understandable, and grounded in daily experience.

Park described discussions of digital coaching, personalization, dignity, and technology acceptance. These topics drew attention to the gap between developing an interesting system and making it meaningful in a real health or care setting.

She thanked Tobias Kowatsch, Rasita Vinay, Felix Moser, and the CDHI team for hosting the exchange. The visit offered space to share research and explore future collaboration without claiming that the technologies discussed were already proven interventions.
